dedupe_keys.name: a unified multi event windstorm performance testbed for single family residential buildings

description: A Unified Multi-Event Windstorm Performance Testbed for Single-Family Residential Buildings is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by David Roueche, Auburn University (auburn.edu). This project presents a synthesized multi-event WindStorm Performance Dataset (WiSPD). The WiSPD is currently comprised of 4 hurricanes (Harvey (2017), Irma (2017), Michael (2018), and Laura (2020)), and 4 tornadoes (Joplin, MO (2011), Garland-Rowlett, TX (2015), Cookville, TN (2020), and Nashville, TN (2020)), all of which struck in the United States. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-ety5-qv78. Keywords: Reconnaissance, hurricane, tornado, testbed, performance. Published 2023-10-10. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
